result.title: Random Probing for Structural Self-Interactions in Graph Neural Networks
result.summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) fundamentally lack the ability to capture structural properties defined by node self-interactions, such as cycle counts, subgraph centrality, and heat kernel signatures. Existing solutions often rely on computationally expensive higher-order architectures or hand-crafted features. In this work, we introduce DIAL, a message-passing layer that gives nodes access to graph structure through the diagonal of graph-derived operators. Our approach uses randomized probing to provide nodes with learnable, permutation equivariant access to diagonal entries. We prove that our approach can express important structural features, including cycle counts, subgraph centrality, and heat kernel signatures. The proposed method can be integrated directly into message passing layers. Experiments on molecular property prediction, cycle counting, and pattern detection demonstrate the effectiveness of DIAL across a range of graph learning tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DIAL 消息传递层，用随机探针让节点以可学习、置换等变的方式访问图算子的对角元，使模型能表达环路计数、子图中心性与热核签名等结构特征，并在分子性质预测、环路计数与模式检测上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但「用随机探针把结构量注入节点状态而非依赖高阶架构」的思路，可能为研究 latent 推理状态如何保留并读取几何/结构证据提供可供核查的线索。
